the-crowd:
Gustave Le Bon subtitled The Crowd a study of the popular mind. The book opens among the titles of a criminology series from the London publisher T. Fisher Unwin, then turns to its subject: the traits of crowds. Le Bon states that his work gives an account of what crowds are like.

He argues that when people gather into a crowd for action, new mental traits appear that differ, at times sharply, from the shared traits heredity gives a race. Organized crowds have always shaped the life of peoples, he says, but never so much as now, when the blind action of crowds replaces the aware activity of single persons. He pledges a purely scientific method, free of schools, doctrines, and regard for the interests his findings may hurt.
